meta.scope: Paraguay batch 5 — Education/health depth, additional departments, social indicators (school attendance, health coverage), and further trade instruments (Chile bilateral, ALADI/ACE network). Completes the ~50-candidate depth target.

candidates.title: Ministerio de Educación y Ciencias (MEC) — education statistics and budget
candidates.description: Ministry responsible for the formal education system. Publishes enrolment, attendance and institutional statistics; major functional allocation in the national budget (constitutionally prioritised).
candidates.notes: Core education node. Budget share is large (often the single largest functional category). Attendance rates from EPHC are high in primary ages but fall in the upper secondary range (~87% for 15–17). Rural–urban gaps persist.

candidates.title: Tasa de asistencia escolar (EPHC)
candidates.description: School-attendance rates for the school-age population derived from the continuous household survey. Key education-outcome indicator complementary to administrative enrolment data.
candidates.notes: High overall attendance (~95% for 5–17) but clear age and rural–urban gradients. Complements the MEC administrative series and links education outcomes to the household-survey system.

candidates.title: Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social (MSPyBS)
candidates.description: Public health ministry responsible for the universal public health network. Primary provider for the large share of the population without formal health insurance.
candidates.notes: Public-provider side of a dual system (public + IPS/private). Continuously cited in health-coverage and access analysis; public spending remains below the OPS/OMS 6%-of-GDP recommendation.

candidates.title: Cobertura de seguro médico / Health-insurance coverage
candidates.description: Share of the population with formal health insurance (IPS or private). Complementary indicator to public-health service statistics.
candidates.notes: Structural coverage gap. Roughly 70% of the population lacks formal insurance and depends on the public system; rural coverage is substantially lower than urban. Recurring policy and inequality theme.

candidates.title: Cuentas de Salud / National Health Accounts
candidates.description: Satellite accounts of health expenditure (public and private) relative to GDP and total current health spending.
candidates.notes: Links the health system to the macroeconomic accounts. Public health spending has risen but remains below regional and OPS benchmarks; private out-of-pocket spending is material.

candidates.title: Departamento de Itapúa — southern agricultural hub
candidates.description: Southern department with significant agricultural production and intermediate-to-higher poverty relative to the capital region.
candidates.notes: Completes the departmental set. Frequently appears in both poverty rankings and agricultural-production geography.

candidates.title: Departamento de Caaguazú — central interior
candidates.description: Central-interior department with elevated poverty incidence and significant rural population.
candidates.notes: High-poverty interior department. Completes the set of departments that test the statistical hierarchy under elevated deprivation.

candidates.title: ACE 35 MERCOSUR–Chile / Acuerdo Comercial Chile–Paraguay
candidates.description: Economic complementarity agreement and the modernised bilateral Chile–Paraguay commercial agreement (in force 2024). Preferential access and updated disciplines on services, digital trade, SPS, TBT, etc.
referenced_by: MIC trade-agreement pages and origin-certificate guidance
Export strategy for the Chilean market
candidates.notes: Important Pacific-facing instrument. The 2024 bilateral modernisation deepens the older ACE 35 relationship with contemporary disciplines.

candidates.title: Red ALADI / Acuerdos de Complementación Económica
candidates.description: Network of ALADI economic-complementarity agreements (ACE) that underpin preferential trade with Chile, Bolivia, Mexico, Peru, Colombia and other partners beyond the core MERCOSUR quartet.
candidates.notes: Broader Latin American preferential architecture. Continuously cited as the legal base for preferential access outside the four MERCOSUR members.

candidates.title: Coeficiente de Gini / Income inequality
candidates.description: Official Gini coefficient of income inequality calculated from EPHC income data. Companion indicator to the monetary-poverty series.
candidates.notes: Structural inequality measure. Complements the poverty headcount and is published alongside the annual poverty results.

proposed_edges.basis: School-attendance rates are derived from the continuous household survey.
Survey-based attendance complements administrative enrolment and institutional statistics from MEC.
IPS affiliation is a primary component of formal health-insurance coverage.
The large uninsured population depends on the public health network administered by MSPyBS.
National Health Accounts are compiled under the health-ministry statistical framework.
The Chile agreement underpins preferential access and origin rules for bilateral trade.
The ALADI/ACE network structures preferential access to multiple Latin American partners.
The Gini coefficient is computed from the same income distribution underlying the poverty estimates.
Itapúa’s poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
Caaguazú’s elevated poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
